title: Fix power right-associativity and unary minus precedence in expr evaluator
prompt:
Fix the bugs in `expr_eval/` (`lexer.py`, `parser.py`):
1. Support the `**` (exponentiation) operator, which must be **right-associative** (`2 ** 3 ** 2 == 512`).
2. Unary minus has lower precedence than `**` (`-2 ** 2 == -4`, while `(-2) ** 2 == 4`), and higher precedence than `*` / `/` (`-3 * 2 == -6`).
3. Support integer division `//` and modulo `%` at the same precedence as `*` and `/`.
Run `pytest` to verify.
